newsitem.title: UK: Siemens UK head confident on semiconductors.
newsitem.headline: Siemens UK head confident on semiconductors.

text.p: The head of Siemens AG's British unit, which last year started building a 1.1 billion stg semi- conductor plant in northern England just as the global price of microchips plunged, said on Thursday he was confident the market would support full plant expansion in line with group plans.

The North Tyneside factory, due to start production in August, "will be utilised fully as soon as the market comes back," Juergen Gehrels, chief executive of Siemens Holdings Plc, the UK arm of the German industrial giant, told a news briefing.
He was commenting on recent press reports that Siemens may struggle to bring the plant up to full operation due to market pressures.

"I think the question as to when it will be fully utilised will be dependent on the market, but one doesn't have to have too much imagination to see that this will happen in the next two years," Gehrels said.

He described last year's drop in semiconductor prices by as much as 75 percent as exceptional and said this year the feeling was "The market will come back again". Initially, the factory will employ 750 people by the end of September 1997 and at that stage its output will be less than a third of its full planned capacity.
Siemens has said the investment is intended to give 1,500 jobs after an expansion of production over two phases.
